_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-10 · SkyDeck — the three "busy" CAC slides turned out to be screenshots, and they were quietly cutting off their own course lists.
_status: The CAC apprenticeship deck is rebuilt and scripted, ready for the 13th. The three pathway slides were not really a design problem — each one was a single flat picture, so none of the text could be edited, searched or read aloud by a screen reader, and the course tables inside them ran off the bottom of the slide where nobody could see them. They are now built properly out of real shapes, in the deck's own fonts and colours, and each one reveals itself in three clicks: the road, then who does what, then what it is worth. The long course lists moved to two appendix pages where they fit. Crystal has a script for every slide and a printed run sheet, timed to thirteen minutes inside the fifteen-minute slot, with every figure pulled fresh from the dashboard this morning. Two things need a person before the meeting: two of the course lists do not add up to the unit totals printed beside them (because of that clipping), and one striking statistic about apprentices dropping out did not come from us — and the agency it is attributed to will be sitting in the room. Everything else on this list is unchanged from yesterday.

items.text: Before the 13th: two course lists in the CAC deck do not add up to the unit totals printed next to them. Carpentry shows twelve courses worth 20 units against 26 claimed; Cerritos shows fifteen worth 31.5 against 38 claimed. American River is exactly right at 29.5, so this is not a counting mistake — the original pictures cut off the bottom rows. Santiago Canyon and Cerritos need to send the full lists. Until they do, the appendix pages carry a printed warning so nobody quotes a number without it.

Before the 13th: the line that 44% of California apprentices withdraw before finishing is a powerful argument, but it did not come from our dashboard — it reaches us second hand, credited to DAS. DAS will be in the audience. Either check it with them beforehand or say out loud that it is their figure rather than stating it as ours. It is flagged three times in the pack.

Five colleges now have a suggested counselling address, but nobody has been able to open their web pages to check it — the network blocks them from here. Each needs about ten seconds in a browser to confirm. Start with Palomar, which runs a separate behavioural-health department that must not be the one we use, and College of the Canyons, where we found nothing usable at all.

Two decisions before the college page can be built: which funding scenario should colleges see (there are two, with different percentages AND different advice), and which year. Year 2 currently has no advice written against it at all, so only Year 1 works today.
Twenty-three pieces of real feedback on Sierra are waiting to be read, nine of them thumbs-down. The oldest has been sitting since 1 July. The robot rows that used to drown this list are gone.

Fourteen colleges have no contact in MAP and we have a suggested one for each. Send them to the MAP team to accept or reject. (Not 56 — the other 42 already have a contact in MAP, so there is nothing to decide there.)

Send Malone the dataset request. Two versions exist — docs/map_dataset_sql_for_malone.md gives him ready-to-run SQL (no view needed), docs/map_custom_report_request_for_malone.md asks for one view name. IMPORTANT correction: we already HAVE the disposition data (Sam checked — it came in via his Access import and is 100% complete). What is missing is only a DAILY refresh, so the college page can be built now and simply states how old its numbers are.
Four colleges publish no usable address at all for a credit question. These need a human to make a call, not another search.
The college contact-refresh cadence was decided in June and still has not run once. Owners are all assigned now, so this is the one governance item with nothing behind it.
Build the college-facing briefing on the same engine as the queue — a college picks itself and a role and gets a rendered briefing, never a blank chat box.

The fifty-two colleges that do have a CPL Assistant were never checked for a student contact, and that check can no longer be done by a session — the college websites are unreachable from here. Decide who does it: a person, or a differently-configured automated run.
Build the college briefing against the live funding settings, not the copy baked into the code — they disagree. Reuse the queue's existing ranking engine rather than writing a second one.

Your Obsidian graph view went blank for about two weeks. It is working again now, but only because the vault got 100x smaller today - the setting that likely contributed is still set the way it was. In graph view, click the gear, open Forces, and drag Link distance from 250 down to about 30. It takes five seconds, you will see the effect immediately, and it stops the graph drifting off-screen again as the vault grows back.

In the CPLBrain repo: Settings, then General, then tick 'Automatically delete head branches'. It is the same setting already on the project tracker. Without it, finished branches linger and every Claude session gets a false 'you have unpushed work' warning that costs a few minutes to disprove. One click, permanent.
